title: R(5,20) >= 427 and R(5,21) >= 447: Ramsey graphs on 426 and 446 vertices
description:
A graph on 426 vertices with no K5 and no independent set of size 20, and a graph on 446 vertices with no K5 and no independent set of size 21. They raise the lower bounds for the Ramsey numbers R(5,20) to 427 (from 426 in version 1.0 and 424 in the survey) and R(5,21) to 447 (from 445). The release also keeps the 425-vertex graph of version 1.0 (R(5,20) at least 426) as history.

Both are built by Theorem 3 of Xu, Shao and Radziszowski (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 25 (2011)) from Mathon's 384-vertex cubic-residue graph and complements of graphs from B. D. McKay's lists, with common induced subgraphs (18 and 20 vertices) found by search under the full Theorem 3 condition: every K4 of the common part has exactly two vertices in each of the two parts. The clique side is checked directly by two independently written exact programs; the independent-set side follows from the theorem, whose hypotheses are machine-checked, and has also been searched directly by finished exact programs (two different programs for the R(5,20) graphs, one for the 446-vertex graph). Best public bounds we could find as of 24 November 2026.
release_notes:
v1.1: R(5,20) >= 427 from a new 426-vertex graph, Theorem 3 with an 18-vertex common part (18 copies of K4, each split 2 and 2 between parts of 10 and 8 vertices). The 425-vertex graph of v1.0 stays as history. R(5,21) >= 447 is unchanged.
New: R5_20_426.txt, its inputs, build and verification code extended, logs of the finished direct independence searches (all three graphs).
README corrected: survey item 2.3.h applies only to the 425-vertex graph; search sweep counts added.
The independent-set side rests on the theorem and on the finished direct searches listed in README.md.
